about.title: Crescent City Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Crescent City is a small coastal town, but its shops, motels, and rental properties still owe visitors a reasonably safe environment. When a wet floor, broken step, uneven pavement near 5th Street, or poor lighting causes a fall, the property owner may bear responsibility — but only if the evidence shows they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn people. That's the heart of a California premises liability case. Because Crescent City is compact, many of its businesses rely on security cameras that overwrite footage within days or weeks, which makes acting quickly important. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured residents with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate the fall, gather what's needed, and explain your options — all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Crescent City Fall Victims Reach Out to Us

items.title: Notice Is the Core Issue
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or repeat incidents that establish that notice.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many local businesses recycle surveillance footage quickly, so getting a preservation request out fast matters. An independent attorney can send that request before footage of the fall is gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue a claim even if you're partly at fault for the fall — your share of fault would just reduce, not eliminate, potential recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Crescent City?
items.answer: In general, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity — a city building or park, for example — that deadline is much shorter, often just six months to submit a claim. It's worth having an attorney check the ownership of the property early.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Rt 101 or near L Street and there's no video?
items.answer: A lack of camera footage doesn't automatically end a claim. Witness statements, incident reports, photos of the hazard, and maintenance or complaint records can still help establish that the owner knew or should have known about the condition. An independent attorney can help figure out what evidence is realistically available.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service — we're not a law firm, and we don't charge you to be connected with an independent attorney in our network. Attorneys who take premises liability cases typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.
